title: Pop tunes and taking any recording date
summary: Dance notes bands always had to play weak pop tunes; Edison says he took any date as a business.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: The only trouble, it's always had this relationship with pop music, you know, and that's the damaging thing because, you know, like in the '30s, when all those great bands, they still had to play all these lousy tunes.
Oh, yeah. Well, they're not as lousy as they write today.
Those tunes they have to play now.
Well, like I was talking about yesterday with Billie Holiday, they say, 'Well, these tunes are dogs,' but they're not nearly as bad as --
Gee whiz. And you know, the Donna Summers, the Helen Reddys, the Elton Johns.
Do you play on any of those dates?

Oh, I used to. It was just going to the bank. That's all I looked at it, you know, that was my business. So if you get a call, you never know who you're going to record with, you know? Just go and just do the date. Just like a doctor. When he has a patient, he doesn't know what color it is or what the case -- what he's going to run into, you know? So I just go to the date and whoever's there, I just record with them, you know?
